title: LLM Inference & GPU Performance Engineer
text:
I build efficient inference systems, from CUDA C++ and Triton kernels to LLM scheduling, KV-cache management, and compiler performance analysis. I hold an M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Purdue University (May 2026), specializing in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. I am seeking LLM Inference Engineer, Performance Engineer, and GPU Kernel Engineer roles.
My work connects operator-level optimization with serving latency, throughput, and memory efficiency. I implement, validate against reference outputs, and profile before drawing conclusions. My benchmarks use explicit workload shapes, warmup and steady-state timing, and appropriate PyTorch or cuBLAS baselines; I investigate regressions as carefully as speedups.

title: LLM Inference & GPU Performance Engineer
text:
Selected Work

GPU kernels for LLM inference: FP32 RMSNorm and GEMV/small-M GEMM in CUDA C++ and Triton, including residual fusion that reduced seven eager PyTorch launches to one. Passed 80/80 backend-shape checks.
nano-vLLM inference runtime: Continuous batching, chunked prefill, paged KV storage, and prefix caching. Measured 3.84x output throughput versus single-sequence scheduling on 12 mixed-length Qwen3-0.6B requests.
PyTorch compiler performance: FX capture, graph breaks, fusion, and correctness-checked LLM benchmarks. Reduced an eight-step Qwen2.5-0.5B FP32 decode from 97.9 to 66.8 ms with CUDA Graphs disabled.
FlashAttention-2 in Triton: Forward attention with online softmax, FP16 MHA/GQA, and causal masking; validated 60/60 cases against PyTorch SDPA.
MobileCLIP2 on Qualcomm QNN: PyTorch-to-ONNX-to-QNN deployment with 794/794 profiled operations on NPU and image/text P90 latencies of 14.51/3.99 ms on the S22 Family target.

title: LLM Inference & GPU Performance Engineer
text:
Background
At Purdue, I led IE 332 labs for 75 students covering machine learning, data pipelines, SQL, and backend development (August 2023 to December 2025). As a Data Science Researcher with Cisco and Purdue Data Mine (January to May 2024), I built forecast selection and ensembling methods for 10,000+ products, improving cost-weighted prediction accuracy by 3%.
My technical toolkit includes Python, C++, CUDA, Triton, CuTe DSL, CUTLASS, PyTorch, torch.compile, and ONNX. I use PyTorch Profiler, Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, and Perfetto to connect runtime behavior to hardware bottlenecks, with additional interests in MLIR, XLA, TVM, quantization, and distributed inference.

title: Edge AI & Deployment
text:
Export & Graph Optimization
Built a static PyTorch → ONNX opset-16 → QNN pipeline with FastViT reparameterization and normalization, SDPA, and EOS rewrites. Correcting preprocessing raised fractional R@10 from 0.043 to 0.897.

title: Edge AI & Deployment
text:
Accuracy & Device Validation
Validated all 56 image and 211 text device outputs at unchanged R@10 of 0.897470, with image/text cosine similarity of 0.999863/0.999998.
Rejected calibrated W8A16 QDQ after image cosine similarity dropped to 0.811, and isolated an S22/v69 DLC-composition failure. These checks informed the deployment choice alongside latency measurements.
